                    ### Question
                    A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he was involved in a motorcycle collision. He was not wearing a helmet. Physical examination shows left periorbital ecchymosis. A CT scan of the head shows a fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure. Physical examination of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Decreased sense of smell
opb. Numbness of the left cheek
opc. Preserved left lateral gaze
opd. Absent left corneal reflex
ope. Complete loss of vision of the left eye

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the case of a fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure, the cranial nerves most likely affected are III, IV, V1, and VI. This can lead to ophthalmoplegia, which includes impaired eye movements and potentially an absent corneal reflex due to V1 involvement. Numbness of the left cheek is unlikely as it involves the maxillary branch (V2) of the trigeminal nerve, which is not affected by superior orbital fissure compression. Preserved left lateral gaze is unlikely due to potential impairment of the abducens nerve (VI), which controls lateral rectus muscle movement. Complete loss of vision is unlikely as the optic nerve (II) is not typically involved in superior orbital fissure syndrome. Decreased sense of smell is also unlikely as the olfactory nerve (I) is not involved. Therefore, the most likely finding is an absent left corneal reflex due to V1 involvement.
